title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented University of Miami rituals, from the Lake Osceola boat burn to Sebastian’s graduation reveal.

cards.title: Watch the Boat Burn at Lake Osceola
cards.subtitle: Homecoming • Lake Osceola
cards.notes: Attend the Homecoming boat-burning ceremony from the Lake Osceola viewing area. The official account records its 1956 start and the mast-fall game-day legend.
cards.short_summary: A student-led Homecoming fire ritual with a football omen attached.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Miami describes the boat-burning ceremony as a student-led tradition passed down since 1956; its legend says a mast that falls before the boat sinks predicts a Hurricanes Homecoming win.
cards.source_title: Boat Burning Ceremony and Fireworks Show
cards.access_notes: Occurs as part of University Homecoming programming; consult the current Homecoming schedule for attendance details.

cards.title: Join the Hurricane Howl
cards.subtitle: Homecoming • Coral Gables Campus
cards.notes: Look for Hurricane Howl on the Homecoming schedule, then stay for the linked boat-burning and fireworks traditions. It is documented in University coverage of Homecoming.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming rally tradition that leads into Lake Osceola festivities.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Miami’s Frost School publication identifies Hurricane Howl, boat burning, and the Homecoming fireworks display as traditional festivities.
cards.access_notes: Presented during Homecoming; confirm the current year’s date and location through University event listings.

cards.title: Spot the Iron Arrow Tapping Procession
cards.subtitle: Iron Arrow Honor Society • Coral Gables Campus
cards.notes: If a public campus procession is announced, observe respectfully from open areas. The society’s documented tapping practice recognizes members chosen for five stated qualities.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial selection ritual for the University’s highest honor society.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Miami documentation says Iron Arrow members assemble twice yearly to select tappees, then conduct a drum-accompanied procession and tap each new member with the Iron Arrow.
cards.source_title: University of Miami Medical Campus Tour
cards.access_notes: Membership and ceremonies are society-administered; view only where the procession is publicly accessible.

cards.entity_name: University of Miami Class Ring Ceremony
cards.title: Recite the Ring Oath
cards.subtitle: Class Ring Ceremony • Coral Gables Campus
cards.notes: Ring recipients can follow Alumni Association instructions for the annual ceremony, ring processional, Ring Oath, and reception. Guest eligibility is set by the event.
cards.short_summary: An annual spring ritual for recipients of the University’s official ring.
cards.evidence_claim: A University of Miami program describes the official Class Ring Ceremony as an annual spring event where recipients receive rings, join a processional, and recite the Ring Oath.
cards.access_notes: For ring recipients and invited guests; confirm current eligibility, registration, and ring purchase requirements with the Alumni Association.

cards.title: Mark Graduation at Senior Mwambo
cards.subtitle: Multicultural Student Affairs • Shalala Student Center
cards.notes: Graduating students and families can check the University calendar for the Senior Mwambo ceremony, a rite-of-passage celebration established at UM in 1992.
cards.short_summary: A University-specific graduation rite honoring community, culture, and transition.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Miami calls Senior Mwambo a longstanding tradition, established in 1992, that honors graduates’ achievements, heritage, and transition to advanced study and professional life.
cards.source_title: UMBAS | Senior Mwambo with Multicultural Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: For graduating students, families, and invited community members; use the University calendar for the next ceremony’s details.

cards.title: See Sebastian’s Seniors Reveal Themselves
cards.subtitle: Commencement • Sebastian the Ibis
cards.notes: Watch commencement closely: graduating student performers traditionally cross the stage in Sebastian’s oversized Ibis feet, publicly revealing their mascot role.
cards.short_summary: The people inside the mascot suit wait until graduation to step into view.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Miami Athletics reports that a tradition developed in which Sebastian performers reveal their identities at graduation by walking across the stage in Ibis feet and jersey.
cards.access_notes: Visible during commencement ceremonies; attendance and guest procedures are set by the University’s commencement office.

cards.title: Learn the C-A-N-E-S Spell-Out
cards.subtitle: Hurricanes sporting events • Sebastian the Ibis
cards.notes: At a Hurricanes event, follow Sebastian and the crowd through the five-letter C-A-N-E-S spell-out. Athletics traces the ritual to the Miami Maniac era.
cards.short_summary: A body-letter cheer that Sebastian adopted and still performs at Hurricanes events.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Miami Athletics states that Sebastian the Ibis adopted the C-A-N-E-S spell-out, a ritual that still stands at Hurricanes sporting events.
cards.access_notes: Join only where event staff permit fan participation; game tickets or venue admission may be required.

cards.title: Start at ’Cane Kickoff
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation • Coral Gables Campus
cards.notes: Incoming first-year and transfer students should use orientation instructions for Cane Kickoff, the University’s signature program for beginning a UM experience.
cards.short_summary: The University’s official welcome week for new Canes.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Miami identifies Cane Kickoff as its signature orientation program for first-year and transfer students and says it introduces new students to campus traditions.
cards.source_title: Cane Kickoff 2025: Welcome to the U
cards.access_notes: Intended for incoming students; follow Orientation and Commuter Student Involvement directions for required sessions and registration.

cards.title: Rub the U Before a Big Moment
cards.subtitle: The U Statue • The Rock, Coral Gables Campus
cards.notes: Stop at the orange-and-green U statue by the Rock before an exam, interview, or game if you want to take part in the student good-luck custom.
cards.short_summary: A campus statue became a luck ritual immediately after its Homecoming unveiling.
cards.evidence_claim: The Miami Hurricane reported that, after the U statue’s 2012 Homecoming unveiling, students were encouraged to rub it for good luck before exams, athletic events, interviews, and other important occasions.
cards.source_title: Statue revealed at Homecoming opening ceremonies
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; respect the surrounding grounds and any temporary access controls.

cards.title: Watch the Canes Run Through the Smoke
cards.subtitle: Miami Hurricanes football • Hard Rock Stadium
cards.notes: Arrive before kickoff for the football team’s smoke-tunnel entrance. University Athletics describes the white-smoke run as a famed Miami football tradition.
cards.short_summary: A pregame team entrance through a cloud of white smoke.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Miami Athletics describes running through the smoke as a Miami football tradition and reported in 2023 that Hurricanes players were preparing to return through the famed white smoke at Hard Rock Stadium.
cards.source_title: It’s the Beginning of a Long Journey
cards.access_notes: A football game ticket and stadium entry are generally required; arrive before kickoff because the entrance occurs pregame.
